name: MD-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Kweisi Mfume running for reelection
Republican challenger with no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Mfume holds a heavily Democratic Baltimore-area seat with a strong cash advantage, while Collier shows no measurable campaign infrastructure or outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win.
model.watch: Any unexpected Mfume scandal or retirement, or a surge of outside Republican spending, would be the only realistic path to tightening this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 7th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, anchored in Baltimore. Kweisi Mfume, a longtime incumbent, is running for reelection with a solid financial cushion of roughly $700,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Scott Collier, has reported no fundraising and no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent. With the district's D+31 lean and the incumbent's advantages, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with the only uncertainty being the exact size of the winning margin.
